messages:
anya: Quick sync — proposal for how route-level model pinning should interact with quotas, capacity, and compatibility. TL;DR: we need clear semantics (hard vs soft pin), a deterministic fallback chain, and telemetry for pin-misses.

lucas: What's the primary failure mode we're trying to avoid? unclear fallback behaviour when dedicated capacity or customer quota blocks the pinned model.

anya: Exactly. Example: a customer pins /api/chat -> alias:redwood-3b-v2@2026-02. If that model is temporarily out of capacity or the customer's token quota would exceed, we either fallback to a different model silently (bad), or return 429 (also bad for soft-pins). Need explicit policy.

cheng: Two-mode proposal: `hard` pins = absolute (no fallback, return 429 if unavailable); `soft` pins = preferred, gateway may route to fallback models by policy. Add header override so infra/sales can force a behaviour: `X-RW-Model-Pin: hard|soft`.

sarah: From a UX perspective console must show per-route effective model, pin_mode, and a small timeline of pin-misses / fallbacks (count + % traffic). Provide a link when a hard pin returns 429 with suggested remediation.

anya: Telemetry: emit `pin_miss` event with keys: route, requested_alias, resolved_model, reason=(capacity|quota|compatibility), timestamp. Also sample last-10 request headers for debugging (opt-in).

dev-bot: Policy syntax suggestion (proto):
```
match: path.startsWith("/api/chat")
pin: "alias:redwood-3b-v2@2026-02"
pin_mode: soft
fallbacks:
  - condition: capacity < 0.8
    candidate: "alias:redwood-3b-lite@2026-02"
  - condition: compatibility(tokenizer) == true
    candidate: "alias:redwood-3b-q4"
```

lucas: Two notes: 1) `capacity` check must be per-customer per-region. 2) `compatibility(tokenizer)` is crucial — we must avoid swapping to a model with an incompatible tokenizer or output schema.

cheng: Compatibility matrix idea: maintain a lightweight registry with fields: model_id, tokenizer_hash, output_schema_version, quantization_flags, runtime_requirements. Gateway checks `tokenizer_hash == requested_tokenizer_hash` and `output_schema_version >= required_version` before accepting fallback. We'll host a cached copy in the model-catalog service.

sarah: UX for rollouts: when changing alias to a new version, console should support canary percent, pin_window (how long the pin sticks), and auto-rollback if `pin_miss_rate > X%` or if fallback_latency_ratio > Y. Show predicted cost delta for the canary.

anya: Quotas question: if routing to the pinned model would exceed the customer's billing/quota soft-limit, do we fail or fallback? Policy: for soft pins, fallback. For hard pins, return 429 + a clear error code `model_pin.quota_exceeded`. Console should show the offending quota and a one-click topo to increase quota.

lucas: Implement plan: gateway evaluates route -> resolves alias -> reads pin_mode -> consults model-catalog cache -> consults capacity & quota (fast cache & fallback to async) -> runs compatibility checks -> select model or run fallback chain. All decision work must be < 5ms median to avoid adding P99 latency.

cheng: We'll need new metrics: `pinned_fallbacks_total`, `pinned_failures_429_total{reason}`, `pinned_models_in_violation_gauge`, and histogram `fallback_latency_ratio`. Also traces to link request -> decision path.

sarah: Also add an API: `GET /v1/resolve?route=/api/chat&headers=...` that returns what model WOULD be used (without executing) for CI and console preview. Useful for customers to validate pins.

anya: For compatibility tests, we should run lightweight tokenization/roundtrip tests in CI when new model versions are onboarded. If tokenizer changes, alias update should require an explicit flag `allow_tokenizer_change=true` and console must show breaking changes.

lucas: I'll take the compatibility matrix + CI tokenization tests. :thumbsup:

cheng: I'll own gateway changes and perf budget.

sarah: I'll prototype the console screens for pin modes, telemetry, and canary UX.

anya: I'll draft the spec and PR for policy syntax. Can we aim for a spike + perf prototype next week?

dev-bot: Created ticket RW-1329: "route model pinning: semantics, telemetry, and console UX".

lucas: One more micro-debate: should we allow route-level transforms to change request tokens (e.g., system prompt expansion) after pin-resolution? That can affect quotas. If allowed, we must calculate pre/post token estimates and check quotas against worst-case.

anya: Good catch — quantify transforms pre-route and account for worst-case in quota checks. I'll add that to the spec.

cheng: OK. Will add a checkbox in the gateway for "account_for_transform_overhead".

sarah: Sounds good — will sync after the spike.

anya: Thanks all. Short PR coming.
